Paper Comparison: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

Introduces Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices into transformer layers, cutting trainable parameters by 10,000x with no added inference latency.
FlashAttention-3: Fast and Memory-Efficient Attention with IO-Awareness

Presents an IO-aware exact attention algorithm with asynchronous block-wise computation and improved memory tiling that reduces HBM accesses 3-5x and achieves 2.1x speedup over FlashAttention-2 while enabling 128K-token context.
Sparse Mixture of Experts for Scalable Transformer Models

Replaces dense feed-forward layers with sparsely-activated expert layers routed by a learned gating mechanism, scaling model capacity 8-64x at constant per-token cost with an improved load-balancing loss to prevent expert collapse.
Efficient Transformers via Token Merging and Pruning

Proposes a unified framework that merges or prunes redundant tokens in intermediate transformer layers using bipartite matching, cutting processed tokens by up to 60% while preserving accuracy within 0.3% on ImageNet without retraining.
Quantization-Aware Training for Efficient Transformer Inference

Introduces a quantization-aware training framework with learnable step sizes, mixed-precision quantization and a low-bias gradient estimator, shrinking model size 4x and inference latency 2.8x within 0.5 perplexity of the full-precision baseline.
